summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) is heavily investing in artificial intelligence to scale its applications across various enterprise functions, from product innovation to back-office operations. summary: An analysis by the Cincinnati Business Courier ranked Dr. August Troendle, CEO of Medpace Holdings, as the top-performing CEO among Greater Cincinnati public companies based on total shareholder return relative to the S&P 500 during his tenure. summary: Unilever's new CEO, Hein Schumacher, announced a plan to revive the company's struggling market share by focusing on top brands and ruling out major acquisitions, a strategy that underwhelmed investors as shares fell. summary: Colgate-Palmolive (COL) reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings after raising prices by an average of 9.5% globally. summary: Procter & Gamble has launched a significant innovation in its Pampers Swaddlers line, introducing a "Blowout Barrier" designed to prevent up to 100% of leaks. summary: Berkshire Hathaway fully exited its small position in Procter & Gamble, likely due to consolidating its portfolio and P&G's premium valuation compared to other opportunities like Apple. summary: Procter & Gamble announced it would record up to $2.5 billion in charges over two fiscal years, including a $1.3 billion non-cash impairment charge on its Gillette business and $1 billion to $1.5 billion related to restructuring operations in Argentina and Nigeria. summary: Procter & Gamble Co. announced charges of up to $2.5 billion over the next two fiscal years for restructuring operations in certain enterprise markets, including Argentina and Nigeria, and a non-cash impairment related to its Gillette business. summary: Jim Cramer remains confident in Procter & Gamble (PG) despite its underperformance in 2023 compared to the S&P 500. summary: This article outlines five reasons why investors may want to avoid buying Procter & Gamble stock (PG), despite its reputation as a safe consumer products company. summary: Procter & Gamble continues to demonstrate strong pricing power as consumers accept higher prices for its premium brands like Tide, despite a slip in sales volumes. title: Founding families press Procter & Gamble Co. to save the world’s forests
summary: Descendants of Procter & Gamble's founding families are urging the company to adopt stronger environmental policies, particularly concerning deforestation linked to its wood pulp and palm oil sourcing. This generational quest aims to redefine P&G's environmental stewardship and address climate change.

title: Environmental protesters target P&G CEO's $2.8M house in Covington Tuesday
summary: Environmental protesters are targeting Procter & Gamble CEO Jon Moeller's Covington home with a mobile billboard to protest the company's forestry and sourcing policies ahead of its annual shareholder meeting. summary: Procter & Gamble is taking a $1.3 billion accounting charge on its Gillette business, nearly two decades after acquiring the shaving giant for $54 billion in 2005. title: Procter & Gamble descendants ask shareholders to shake up the board over deforestation
summary: Descendants of Procter & Gamble founders, who are also shareholders, are urging fellow shareholders to vote against four board nominees, including CEO Jon Moeller, due to the company's perceived insufficient efforts to combat deforestation. title: Storied former P&G soap factory shutting down in March
summary: The St. Bernard Soap Co., a former Procter & Gamble subsidiary and contractor known for producing iconic bar soaps like Ivory, will cease operations by mid-March, leading to 118 job losses. title: Patrick Industries buys Minnesota manufacturer Sportech for $315 million
summary: Patrick Industries has acquired Sportech, a Minnesota-based manufacturer of vehicle component parts for motorcycles, snowmobiles, and ATVs, for $315 million. title: P&G beauty line needs a makeover, analysts say
summary: Analysts suggest that Procter & Gamble's beauty care business, which accounts for nearly a quarter of its revenue, needs a significant turnaround to reignite sales growth. title: P&G: ‘Now Is Not The Time To Be Pulling Back On Investments In Marketing.’

title: Coca-Cola pilot removes labels from Sprite bottles to ease recycling
summary: Coca-Cola has launched a limited trial of label-less 500mL Sprite and Sprite Zero bottles in British supermarkets to further ease recycling and reduce packaging material. The initiative follows the company's 2022 move to switch Sprite bottles from green to clear PET to improve bottle-to-bottle circularity. The company aims for all its packaging to be recyclable by 2025 and to cut 3 million metric tons of virgin plastic by 2025 from a 2020 baseline.

title: 2027 the Target for Transition Away from 1D GTIN, Toward Digital Link 2D Barcodes
summary: The packaging industry is targeting 2027 for a significant transition from the traditional 1D GTIN barcode to the more versatile Digital Link 2D barcode. This shift, driven by increasing consumer demand for information, regulatory requirements, and supply chain traceability needs, will enable a single QR code to provide different information to various stakeholders (consumers, retailers, supply chain partners). The "Sunrise 2027" program aims to prepare the necessary infrastructure, primarily software changes, for this industry-wide adoption.

title: In Depth: The power of prestige beauty
summary: Despite global challenges like a pandemic and cost-of-living crisis, the prestige beauty market continues to thrive, driven by consumer desire for small luxuries and emotional purchases. Major beauty companies like Shiseido, Unilever, and Estée Lauder are heavily investing in this sector through acquisitions and strategic developments, recognizing its robust growth potential and attractive profit margins compared to mass-market brands. This trend, often linked to the "lipstick effect," is expected to continue with more investments and acquisitions in 2024 and beyond.

title: Waldencast Names Manuel Manfredi as CFO
summary: Waldencast plc announced the appointment of Manuel Manfredi as its new Chief Financial Officer, effective April 1, 2024. Manfredi brings nearly 25 years of financial leadership experience in the beauty and consumer products industries, most recently serving as CFO for L’Oréal Spain and Portugal. Michel Brousset, Waldencast's CEO, will act as interim CFO until Manfredi's start date, succeeding Philippe Gautier who is departing the company.

title: Artificial Intelligence at Procter & Gamble
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) is scaling its AI initiatives across various departments, focusing on clear business purposes, organizational AI fluency, and standardized development. The article highlights two key AI use cases: supply chain optimization using the KNIME platform for predictive analytics and consumer behavior analysis through real-time data from smart products like the Oral B iO toothbrush to inform product development. These applications aim to improve efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance customer satisfaction for the multinational goods corporation.

title: Neighbors oppose P&G expansion at former Iowa City Kirkwood campus
summary: Neighbors in Iowa City are opposing Procter & Gamble's proposed expansion onto the former Kirkwood Community College campus, citing concerns about environmental justice and potential health impacts from increased industrial activity. Residents, including Anne Marie Kraus, fear the expansion will exacerbate existing issues like air pollution and argue that the area, which has a higher percentage of low-income and minority residents, should not be disproportionately affected by industrial development. The Iowa City Council is set to consider rezoning the 6.8-acre property from neighborhood public to general industrial, despite P&G stating they have no immediate plans for the site beyond potential expansion of oral care operations, not chemical production.

title: General Mills rolls out MillsChat, an internal generative AI tool
summary: General Mills has launched MillsChat, a private generative AI tool built on Google's PaLM 2 model, for its employees in the U.S., Canada, U.K., and India. The tool is designed to assist with writing, summarizing, and brainstorming in a secure environment. This initiative reflects General Mills' increasing investment in AI, having grown its data science headcount fortyfold since 2018, and aligns with other food brands like Kraft Heinz, Coca-Cola, and Procter & Gamble that are also integrating generative AI into their operations to improve business outcomes and operational efficiencies despite a challenging consumer landscape.

title: P&G CEO would change debate from 'social justice to winning' to bolster diversity
summary: Procter & Gamble CEO Jon Moeller advocates for reframing the conversation around diversity from "social justice" to "winning" to make a more powerful argument for women and diverse individuals in leadership roles. He emphasized that linking diverse representation to business success is fundamental for attracting and serving a diverse consumer base. Moeller expects that P&G will eventually have a female CEO, acknowledging that a significant portion of their consumer base is women.

title: The Clorox Company Tops Barron’s 2024 List of The 100 Most Sustainable US Companies
summary: The Clorox Company has topped Barron’s 2024 list of the 100 Most Sustainable US Companies for the second consecutive year, achieving a final score of 77 based on 230 environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance indicators. Other notable companies from the beauty, cleaning, and personal care industries, including Procter & Gamble, Ecolab, The Estée Lauder Companies, and Colgate-Palmolive, also made the list. Clorox highlighted its accomplishments in pay equity, ESG governance, board diversity, its climate action plan, renewable energy use, and waste reduction efforts.

title: Nestlé, P&G, and Walmart reveal their 2024 talent retention secrets
summary: Nestlé, Procter & Gamble, and Walmart are focusing on talent retention in 2024 by enhancing employee benefits, offering stock options, and promoting internal growth through structured career development and access to AI tools. P&G, for instance, emphasizes continuous learning within the company, with employees typically taking on five different roles in their first decade. This strategy aims to counteract high job-switching rates and foster a "Big Stay" environment.

title: Kroger and P&G open applications for the 2024 Game Changers Scholarship
summary: Kroger's Columbus Division and The Procter & Gamble Company have opened applications for their 2024 Game Changers Scholarship program. The scholarship aims to support underrepresented female students pursuing higher education in business, science, technical, and liberal arts fields. One local scholarship of $2,000 will be awarded by Kroger, contributing to a national total of over $45,000 for 23 women, administered by the Ohio Foundation of Independent Colleges and Scholarship Management Resources.

title: Procter & Gamble SVP Named Barton School’s Executive-in-Residence
summary: Tadd Fowler, Senior Vice President at Procter & Gamble and an alumnus, has been named the Spring 2024 Executive-in-Residence for the W. Frank Barton School of Business at Wichita State University. He will deliver a public keynote address, mentor students, and guest lecture, discussing P&G's transformation and relevancy. This initiative aims to provide students and the public with insights from a distinguished executive.

title: Microsoft, P&G, Unilever and Walmart among 239 companies to miss net-zero deadline
summary: The Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) has reclassified 239 companies, including Microsoft, P&G, Unilever, and Walmart, as "commitment removed" for net-zero goals because they failed to submit science-based targets for validation within the 24-month deadline. A significant obstacle for these companies is the difficulty in reducing Scope 3 emissions, which relate to indirect emissions from customers and supply chains. Despite the reclassification, these major corporations maintain that they are continuing to pursue aggressive emissions reduction targets and are in various stages of reviewing or updating their strategies to align with SBTi standards, with many still holding near-term validated targets.

title: The First Brands acquisition: Marking 25 years
summary: The article reflects on the 25th anniversary of The Clorox Company's acquisition of First Brands Inc., a pivotal event that doubled Clorox's size and brought iconic brands like Glad and Scoop Away into its portfolio. It highlights the transformation and innovation that followed, including the development of advanced products like Glad's ForceFlex™ and OdorShield® technologies and Scoop Away's enhanced features. The piece also acknowledges the integration of First Brands' facilities and, most importantly, its employees into the Clorox family, celebrating the enduring legacy of the acquisition.

title: Procter & Gamble Brings Relief to Residents Affected by Tornadoes in Ohio and Indiana
summary: Procter & Gamble, in partnership with Walmart and Matthew 25: Ministries, is providing disaster relief to communities in Ohio and Indiana affected by recent tornadoes. Beginning March 18, 2024, at the Church of God in Russells Point, Ohio, they will offer free laundry services via the Tide Loads of Hope Mobile Laundry Unit, hot showers from a dedicated trailer, and distribute personal care kits and cleaning supplies. These services aim to help families and first responders in their recovery efforts.

title: P&G’s Former Chair Bob McDonald: ‘Life Is A Series Of Starting Over’
summary: This article features insights from former P&G CEO and U.S. Secretary of Veterans Affairs, Bob McDonald, as discussed in the Corporate Competitor Podcast with Don Yaeger. McDonald emphasizes the importance of an "abundance mindset" and the confidence to embrace new beginnings throughout life and career. He shares his journey from a high-ranking military career to leading P&G and later the Department of Veterans Affairs, highlighting his purpose-driven approach and leadership philosophy centered on serving others.

title: Dow, Procter & Gamble partnering to develop new recycling technology
summary: Dow and Procter & Gamble have formed a joint development agreement to create a new recycling technology. This initiative aims to efficiently convert hard-to-recycle plastic packaging into near-virgin quality recycled polyethylene with a low greenhouse gas emissions footprint. The partnership seeks to advance a circular economy by enabling the reuse of recycled polymers in consumer packaging.

title: Dow and P&G partner to create new plastics recycling technology
summary: Dow and Procter & Gamble (P&G) have formed a joint development agreement to create new proprietary recycling technology for hard-to-recycle plastic waste. This collaboration aims to convert challenging packaging, including rigid, flexible, and multilayer plastics, into high-quality recycled polyethylene (PE) using a dissolution process. The goal is to produce near-virgin quality PCR PE with reduced greenhouse gas emissions, which P&G plans to integrate into its consumer packaging to foster a circular economy.

title: Rolaids® Bolsters Presence in Convenience Stores Through Strategic Partnership with Lil’ Drug Store Products
summary: Lil’ Drug Store Products (LDSP) has partnered with Procter & Gamble (P&G) to become the primary distributor of Rolaids® to convenience and travel retailers nationwide. This collaboration aims to make Rolaids the #1 antacid brand in the convenience sector by 2028, leveraging P&G's investment and targeting the significant overlap between convenience store consumers and heartburn sufferers. LDSP has already resumed distribution of Rolaids products, which will feature flavor and texture upgrades under P&G's ownership.

title: Kimberly-Clark to reorganize business, incur $1.5 bln in costs
summary: Kimberly-Clark announced a reorganization into three business units to simplify operations and cut costs, expecting to incur about $1.5 billion in related costs over the next three years, with half of that from workforce reductions. The move comes as the company faces waning benefits from price hikes and increased competition from private-label alternatives. The restructuring aims to generate over $3 billion in gross productivity and $500 million in working capital savings, expecting completion by the end of 2024.

title: New Balance President and CEO Joe Preston and Procter & Gamble-Gillette Vice President Karan Dyson to Deliver Commencement Addresses at Bentley University
summary: Bentley University announced that New Balance President and CEO Joe Preston will deliver the keynote address for the undergraduate commencement, and Procter & Gamble-Gillette Vice President Karan Dyson will speak at the graduate commencement. Both executives are recognized for their leadership and will receive honorary Doctor of Commercial Science degrees. The ceremonies, celebrating over 1,500 students, will take place on May 17th and 18th, 2024.

title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Berkshire Hathaway, Procter & Gamble, Adobe, Advanced Micro Devices and AstraZeneca
summary: This Zacks Analyst Blog highlights research reports on major stocks including Berkshire Hathaway, Procter & Gamble, and Adobe, along with Advanced Micro Devices and AstraZeneca PLC. It provides an overview of each company's recent performance, key financial drivers, and potential headwinds. The article emphasizes Zacks Investment Research's stock-picking strategies and their strong historical performance.

title: Dear Younger Self: 3 Lessons From a P&G Executive
summary: Fama Francisco, CEO of Global Baby, Feminine and Family Care at P&G, shares three key lessons learned over her 35-year career. These lessons include persevering when faced with setbacks, embracing one's unique authentic self and flexing different skills, and prioritizing personal well-being to avoid burnout. Her experiences highlight P&G's commitment to employee development and a diverse, inclusive workplace.

title: Cereal giant Post is bringing a distribution center to North Texas
summary: Post Consumer Brands, a division of Post Holdings Inc. (NYSE: POST), known for cereals like Fruity Pebbles and Honeycomb, is establishing a 1.1 million-square-foot distribution center in Wilmer, near Dallas. This move follows the company's expansion, including recent pet food brand acquisitions, and aims to optimize its distribution network. The deal represents the largest industrial lease in the DFW region for 2024 so far.

title: P&G vendió las marcas Magistral y Ariel a Dreamco S.A.
summary: Dreamco S.A. has completed the acquisition of P&G's fabric and dish care business in Argentina, including the brands Magistral and Ariel. This transaction involved the transfer of a plant and distribution center in Pilar, Buenos Aires, along with equipment and specific usage permits. Bruchou & Funes de Rioja advised Dreamco on labor aspects and on securing a syndicated loan from Banco de Galicia and Banco BBVA Argentina for working capital and asset structuring.

title: 2023 Top 100: Why Procter & Gamble’s Beauty Business Grew Across the Board
summary: Procter & Gamble's beauty division experienced significant growth in 2023 across most brands and geographies, despite economic headwinds. The mass hair business showed steady growth, while the Specialty Beauty division, including acquired brands like Mielle Organics and Native, saw sales swell over 70 percent. Olay's skincare innovations contributed to moderate growth, though high-end brand SK-II faced sales declines due to geopolitical factors.

title: Procter & Gamble Co: Disclosure of PFAS-Related Risk Management Practices
summary: A shareholder resolution requests Procter & Gamble to publish a report detailing its management of health and environmental risks associated with PFAS chemicals in its products. This request follows concerns about PFAS detection in Tampax products and the broader health and litigation risks linked to these chemicals. Other personal care companies are already taking steps to minimize PFAS and disclose their efforts.

title: Procter & Gamble's strategic pricing shift should accelerate business growth this year
summary: Procter & Gamble is adjusting its pricing strategy to prioritize volume growth over price increases, responding to inflation-weary consumers. This shift is expected to accelerate business growth, with analysts anticipating improved volumes due to more stable pricing. Wall Street is closely watching P&G's upcoming fiscal 2024 third-quarter earnings report for signs of this strategy's impact.

title: P&G’s stock falls after a sales miss, as baby and health-care volumes declined
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. (P&G) stock fell after the company reported fiscal third-quarter sales that missed forecasts, primarily due to weakness and volume declines in its baby, feminine, and family-care segments. Despite the sales miss, P&G beat quarterly profit expectations and subsequently raised its full-year outlook. Prices increased at the slowest rate in over two years, while volume remained flat for the second consecutive quarter.

title: Procter & Gamble Stock Slips Despite Earnings Beat as Q3 Sales Miss Estimates
summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) reported third-quarter earnings that surpassed estimates, but revenue fell short of expectations, leading to a slight dip in share price. Despite missing sales estimates, the company maintained its full-year sales growth outlook and increased its EPS projections. Organic sales remained strong across most segments, driven by a 3% price increase.

title: P&G lifts annual profit forecast on strong US consumer demand, easing costs
summary: Procter & Gamble raised its annual profit forecast due to lower commodity costs and continued strong consumer demand, especially in the U.S. and Europe. This comes despite a slight miss on third-quarter net sales expectations. The company also anticipates a higher benefit from favorable commodity costs for fiscal year 2024.

title: Huggies backpedals on ad claims after challenge from Pampers parent P&G
summary: Huggies has retracted certain ad claims following a challenge from Procter & Gamble, the parent company of competitor Pampers. The contested campaign, created by Quality Meats, featured diverse baby bottoms. This development highlights ongoing competitive dynamics in the diaper market.

title: Fifth Third's Somalya on Diversity in Governance
summary: Saema Somalya, deputy general counsel at Fifth Third, emphasizes the critical role of board diversity for corporate competitiveness and economic well-being. She highlights that diverse perspectives are essential for anticipating trends and strengthening oversight, citing Fifth Third's recent addition of Linda Clement-Holmes to its board as an example of a qualifications-based approach leading to increased diversity. Somalya also anticipates increased shareholder activism around board diversity, driven by ESG-focused investing.

title: Inside the 2024 CEW Achiever Awards
summary: The 2024 CEW Achiever Awards honored several prominent women in the beauty industry, including executives from Estée Lauder Cos., Shiseido, Ulta Beauty, and L'Oréal. The event, which drew around 1,000 attendees, also recognized the founder of Supergoop as the keynote speaker, emphasizing themes of passion, purpose, and people. Award recipients shared insights on career growth, the importance of diversity and inclusion, and the impact of mentorship and community in their professional journeys.

title: Procter and Gamble descendant proposes bill to stop the type of animal testing P&G has done
summary: A descendant of Procter & Gamble founders, State Rep. Sara Carruthers (R-Hamilton), has introduced House Bill 495 in Ohio to end most cosmetics animal testing, a practice P&G still engages in despite claiming to be cruelty-free. The bill aims to save animals and boost the cruelty-free cosmetic market, but it faces opposition from medical experts like Sharona Hoffman, who warns of potential negative impacts on medical advancements and research for conditions like burn victims or reconstructive surgeries. While Carruthers argues for cheaper, modern testing alternatives, Hoffman contends that animal studies are crucial for understanding complex biological interactions.

title: West Chester business picks up work after P&G subsidiary closes
summary: ASIC Corp. in West Chester Twp. has taken over the controls piece of the injection molding business after iMFLUX, a Procter & Gamble subsidiary, shut down its Symmes Road operations last year. ASIC, a family-owned business, has hired three former iMFLUX employees and is now responsible for machine sales, training, and service for the control systems, working in conjunction with P&G to advance the imflux technology. They provide replacement parts and integrate the imflux system into various OEM machines for any industry.

title: Changing culture will be key to attracting more women professionals, says AlphaSimplex's Kathryn Kaminski
summary: Kathryn Kaminski of AlphaSimplex Group, who has an engineering background, believes that cultural changes are crucial for attracting more women into the asset management industry. The article highlights this perspective and includes several other financial news snippets covering topics like private credit, endowments, private equity, and pension funds.

title: P&G shifts focus to brands for Paris Olympics ads
summary: Procter & Gamble is changing its advertising strategy for the upcoming Paris Olympics, moving away from its traditional corporate "Thank you, Mom" campaigns to focus on individual brands like Pampers and Gillette. This shift means P&G will launch advertising for over 30 brands, more than ever before, with a particular emphasis on European retailers. The company's chief brand officer stated that this new approach is designed to align with what consumers are more familiar with.

title: P&G Details Cost-Cutting Productivity Enhancements Across Supply Chain, R&D, and Marketing
summary: Procter & Gamble is achieving significant cost savings and productivity gains through digital transformation efforts across its supply chain, R&D, and marketing departments. These enhancements include using technology for faster product reformulation, defect detection in manufacturing, and optimizing marketing strategies. CFO Andre Schultenn expects annual savings of $1.5 billion from supply chain improvements and $500 million from R&D and marketing optimizations.

title: Procter & Gamble announces marketing plans for Paris 2024
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has unveiled its marketing strategy for the Olympic and Paralympic Games Paris 2024, leveraging its status as a Worldwide Olympic and Paralympic Partner. The plan includes Olympic-themed brand marketing, in-store promotions, athlete partnerships, and complimentary products and services for athletes. Brands like Venus and Gillette are launching specific campaigns to highlight product performance in an Olympic context.

title: P&G Honours Suppliers Driving Excellence in Supply Chains
summary: P&G recognized its external business partners at the 2024 Partner of the Year Awards, highlighting their exceptional contributions to supply chains, consumer satisfaction, environmental sustainability, and equality and inclusion. The company awarded five suppliers with the Supplier Impact Award and acknowledged many others for their vital roles in enabling P&G's global operations. Chief Purchasing Officer Ana Elena Marziano emphasized the critical nature of these partnerships for innovation, problem-solving, and mutual business growth.

title: Procter & Gamble, Mondelēz, and Nestlé Are Among 10 of the Leading Consumer Brands Driving Global Deforestation
summary: This article highlights how major consumer brands, including Procter & Gamble, Mondelēz, and Nestlé, are significantly contributing to global deforestation and human rights abuses despite public commitments. A report by the Rainforest Action Network (RAN) graded ten multinational corporations, finding none achieved an 'A' grade, with several performing poorly due to insufficient policies, lack of third-party verification, and continued engagement in practices harmful to forests and communities. The author calls for genuine commitment, transparent reporting, and comprehensive NDPE policies across all supply chains to combat the climate crisis.

title: Procter & Gamble’s Ranya Shamoon brings growth to a tough European baby care market
summary: Ranya Shamoon of Procter & Gamble has successfully driven consistent growth for the company's baby care division in Europe over the past three years. This achievement is particularly notable given the challenging market conditions in the region. The article highlights her role in navigating these difficulties to ensure sustained progress for P&G's baby care portfolio.

title: How Walmart, P&G, General Motors, PepsiCo and other big marketers are spending on Black-owned media
summary: This article discusses how major marketers like Walmart, P&G, General Motors, and PepsiCo are increasing their advertising spend on Black-owned media channels. Based on an Ad Age survey of Black-owned media companies, these brands significantly boosted their investment in 2023. The piece highlights a trend among large companies to support Black-owned media.

title: McCormick adds former Procter & Gamble exec to board
summary: McCormick has appointed a former Procter & Gamble executive to its board of directors, increasing the board's size to 13 members. This article previews the announcement and provides links to related stories about McCormick's executive compensation, new product lines, sales performance, and previous board additions.

title: Campbell Soup Company Shakes Up Supply Chain
summary: Campbell Soup Company is investing $230 million through fiscal year 2026 to modernize its supply chain operations, creating 210 new jobs. This includes significant investments in plants in Maxton, North Carolina; Hanover, Pennsylvania; and Franklin, Wisconsin, along with expanding Goldfish cracker production in Richmond, Utah. The company will also close its Tualatin, Oregon plant and shift production in Jeffersonville, Indiana, as part of its strategy to increase efficiency and drive business growth.

title: Western Companies U-Turn on Russia Exit Plans – FT
summary: Western companies are reconsidering their plans to exit Russia due to high Kremlin-imposed exit costs, difficulties in finding suitable buyers, and a resurgence in consumer activity, according to the Financial Times. While 1,610 foreign companies have left or scaled back operations, 2,175 still remain, with some openly discussing their intentions to stay. Challenges to exiting include mandatory 50% discounts on assets, a 15% exit tax, and the need for Moscow-approved, unsanctioned Russian buyers.

title: Huggies Owner Kimberly-Clark Exits Africa’s Most Populous Market
summary: Kimberly-Clark Corp., the maker of Huggies diapers and Kotex sanitary pads, is ceasing operations in Nigeria after almost 15 years, citing economic developments and a shift in global strategic priorities. This marks its second exit from the country in recent years, following a relaunch in 2022. The departure is part of a larger trend of global conglomerates leaving Nigeria due to currency crises, high operating costs, and unreliable infrastructure.

title: Procter & Gamble to build plant in Poland
summary: Procter & Gamble announced plans to construct a €38m cosmetics plant in Aleksandrow Lodzki, Poland, with an investment of $50m by 2012 and the creation of 300 jobs. This move is part of a broader trend of multinational companies investing in Eastern European markets due to increasing disposable income and booming cosmetics sales. P&G, which already has a strong presence in Poland, expects the factory to be operational by 2009.

title: Aerosol can recycling has confounded consumers. There’s a push to fix that by 2030.
summary: The Aerosol Recycling Initiative, involving the Can Manufacturers Institute and Household and Commercial Products Association, aims to improve aerosol can recycling in the U.S. by 2030. Key goals include achieving an 85% recycling access rate and ensuring 90% of cans are labeled as recyclable with proper instructions. The initiative also seeks to include aerosols in state-wide Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) programs and educate Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs) to overcome perceived fire risks, despite data showing such risks are rare when cans are emptied.

title: Kimberly-Clark Is on a Roll with New Forest Policy and Goals
summary: Kimberly-Clark, maker of Kleenex and Scott tissue products, has announced a new Forests, Land, and Agriculture Policy and a goal to eliminate natural forest fiber from its entire product line. This move sets a higher standard in the industry, aiming to reduce forest degradation, particularly in critical northern forests, and includes commitments to Indigenous communities' rights. The policy puts pressure on competitors like Procter & Gamble and aligns with increasing global regulatory scrutiny on deforestation and forest degradation.

title: P&G Exec Named Top Women in Grocery's CPG Trailblazer
summary: Mindy Sherwood, President of Global Walmart and Chief Sales Officer at Procter & Gamble (P&G), has been recognized as a CPG Trailblazer for Top Women in Grocery. The article highlights her 35-year career at P&G, her leadership philosophy focusing on empowering team members, and her insights on overcoming challenges faced by women in male-dominated industries. Sherwood also shares advice for young professionals starting their careers, emphasizing curiosity, continuous learning, and making a significant impact.

title: Bloomberg: Western Multinationals Fleeing Nigeria Being Replaced by Asian, Turkish Firms
summary: Western multinationals are exiting Nigeria due to economic challenges like currency fluctuations, high inflation, and economic mismanagement, but Asian and local firms are stepping in to fill the void. Companies like Tolaram Group Inc. are succeeding by localizing production and sourcing materials within Nigeria to mitigate currency risks. Despite ongoing difficulties, this shift is creating opportunities for domestic manufacturing and exports to other African countries.

title: Consumer Reports finds unclear ingredients in seven brands of baby wipes
summary: A Consumer Reports investigation revealed that seven out of 15 popular baby wipe brands contain concerning or unclear ingredients, including potentially harmful chemicals and plastics. The report advises consumers to choose plant-based, fragrance-free, biodegradable wipes and warns against leaving wipes in hot environments or flushing them. Following the investigation, a lawsuit was filed against Kirkland (Costco) wipes, alleging high levels of PFAS.

title: P&G brings top TikToker Khaby Lame’s humor stateside with Tubi series
summary: Procter & Gamble is launching a new unscripted reality series called "Khaby Is Coming To America" on Tubi, featuring TikTok star Khaby Lame. The show, co-produced with Group Black, follows Lame as he explores American culture and integrates P&G brands like Tide and Crest. This initiative aims to engage multicultural consumers and amplify diverse voices, building on P&G's "Widen The Screen" program.

title: A Closer Look At Berkshire Hathaway's Chubb Investment
summary: Berkshire Hathaway recently revealed a significant 6.40% stake in Swiss insurer Chubb Ltd., an investment driven by Warren Buffett's longtime affinity for the "collect-now, pay-later" model of the insurance business. This article explores the strategic reasons behind the investment, highlighting Chubb's strong management, robust global presence, underwriting efficiency, and technological innovation, all of which complement Berkshire's existing insurance portfolio. The acquisition suggests potential synergies that could impact the property and casualty insurance industry, though a full buyout of Chubb by Berkshire Hathaway is deemed unlikely in the short term due to Chubb's valuation.

title: VIDEO: ETF of the Week: Invesco S&P 500 Quality ETF (SPHQ)
summary: This article highlights the Invesco S&P 500 Quality ETF (SPHQ), discussed by Todd Rosenbluth of VettaFi and Chuck Jaffe of "Money Life." SPHQ focuses on approximately 100 high-quality S&P 500 companies with strong balance sheets and consistent earnings, outperforming the broader S&P 500. The fund is presented as a potential core replacement or complement for investors seeking diversified exposure to top-tier companies.

title: How Procter & Gamble CEO Moeller plans to use AI
summary: Jon Moeller, Chairman, President, and CEO of Procter & Gamble, emphasizes that the primary goal for implementing AI is to "delight the consumer" by driving superior outcomes for consumers, customers, employees, society, and shareholders. He foresees AI improving quality control, accelerating product innovation, optimizing advertising effectiveness, and boosting employee value through enhanced efficiency. Moeller believes that fostering "digital acumen" among P&G's workforce is crucial for leveraging AI and other new technologies effectively.

title: Dollar Tree Shoppers Share 18 Must-Grab Travel Items for $1.25
summary: Dollar Tree shoppers are sharing money-saving travel essentials available for just $1.25, highlighting many name-brand finds suitable for road trips or checked luggage. The list includes personal care items like travel-size deodorants, lotions, shampoos, and first aid kits, as well as practical accessories like pill organizers and refillable bottles, helping travelers save on expenses. These discoveries from social media users cover a wide range of needs, from hygiene to health, ensuring budget-friendly preparation for any summer getaway.

title: Meet the P&G European Innovators Behind the Innovation
summary: This article highlights two European P&G innovators, Trang Le and Katrien Hellings, discussing their roles and contributions to product development. Trang Le, an R&D Product Research Scientist for Babycare Europe, shares her experience working on Pampers and the latest innovation, the Stop & Protect pocket. Katrien Hellings, an R&D Product Research Scientist for Automatic Dishwashing Europe, reflects on her 25-year career at P&G and the successful introduction of Fairy Platinum Plus.

title: Three Ways We Grow Disability Confidence
summary: P&G celebrates Disability Pride Month by highlighting three ways it promotes disability confidence: fostering an inclusive workplace culture through employee support groups and accessible design, innovating products with features like tactile symbols to meet diverse consumer needs, and maximizing impact through partnerships with organizations dedicated to disability inclusion. The company emphasizes its commitment to creating a world where everyone can thrive.

title: P&G’s Signal Summit Put Market Growth & Value Creation in Focus
summary: P&G's 13th annual Signal Summit focused on driving market growth and value creation in an unpredictable global business environment. Industry leaders from various sectors shared insights on embracing constructive disruption and innovation to achieve business success. Key discussions included the importance of consumer value, product education, authentic marketing, and honest self-assessment for growth.

title: Mondelēz International taps Nestlé, P&G veteran as tech chief
summary: Mondelēz International has appointed Filippo Catalano as its new chief information and digital officer. Catalano, who previously held senior technology roles at Nestlé, Reckitt, and Procter & Gamble, will report directly to CEO Dirk Van de Put. This appointment reflects a broader trend of companies enhancing their tech leadership, with Catalano tasked with driving digital transformation for the global snack company.

title: Procter & Gamble earnings beat estimates, but quarterly sales disappoint as China demand slides
summary: Procter & Gamble reported better-than-expected earnings but missed revenue estimates due to weaker demand in China. Despite overall flat net sales, the company saw a 1% increase in volume for the first time in over two years, driven by grooming, healthcare, and fabric and home care products. Fiscal year 2025 core net earnings per share are projected to be in the range of $6.91 to $7.05, with a reiterated revenue growth outlook of 2% to 4%.

title: P&G Sales Miss Estimates as Price Increases Finally Slow Down
summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) reported quarterly sales that missed analysts' estimates, leading to a significant drop in its shares. This shortfall is attributed to the company slowing its pace of price increases, resulting in the slowest organic sales growth in six years. P&G's forecasts for the current fiscal year's adjusted earnings and revenue were generally in line with market expectations despite the quarterly miss.

title: Jill Pratt To Lead Campbell’s Meals & Beverages Marketing as VP, CMO
summary: Jill Pratt has been appointed as the VP, Chief Marketing Officer for Campbell Soup Company's meals and beverages division. In this role, she will lead the U.S. consumer experience team, focusing on strengthening customer collaborations, attracting new consumers, and modernizing the brand portfolio. Pratt brings extensive CPG marketing experience from previous roles at Heatonist, McCormick & Company, and Procter & Gamble.

title: P&G Announces Results for the Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2024
summary: Procter & Gamble reported strong results for the fourth quarter and fiscal year 2024, driven by excellent execution of its integrated strategy. The company achieved solid growth in organic sales, core EPS, and cash generation, while also increasing market share. P&G anticipates continued strong performance in fiscal year 2025, maintaining its commitment to its established growth strategy.

title: Eastman plans to broaden chemical recycling plant's inputs
summary: Eastman's chemical recycling plant in Kingsport, Tennessee, is nearing 100% capacity and plans to expand its inputs to include a broader range of hard-to-recycle plastics. CEO Mark Costa noted the plant successfully converts "garbage" into high-quality, clear, on-spec polymer. The company is addressing challenges related to non-plastic contaminants in feedstock to enable processing of additional materials.

title: New Marketing Leadership Simmering at Campbell Soup
summary: Campbell Soup Co. has appointed Jill Pratt as SVP and chief marketing officer for its meals and beverages division, where she will lead the U.S. consumer experience team to strengthen customer partnerships and engage consumers for major brands like Campbell’s, Chunky, and Prego. Pratt, with prior experience at McCormick & Co. and Procter & Gamble, will report to Mick Beekhuizen, EVP and president of the division, who expressed confidence in her leadership to accelerate growth. This appointment follows the departure of Linda Lee from the CMO role and comes after Campbell reported strong net sales gains in its third fiscal quarter, partly due to the acquisition of Sovos Brands.

title: CloroxPro launching new line of plant-based disinfecting wipes
summary: CloroxPro is expanding its EcoClean product platform with new plant-based disinfecting wipes. These wipes are designed to meet the rising demand for environmentally friendly cleaners in public facilities, using naturally derived ingredients and a 100% plant-based substrate while still killing 99.9% of germs. The product supports sustainability goals for facilities and Clorox's commitment to reducing virgin plastics and using post-consumer recycled packaging.

title: Alex Keith on Balancing Tradition with Transformation in the Global Beauty Market | P&G
summary: P&G Beauty CEO Alex Keith discusses at ShopTalk Europe how brands like Old Spice and Head & Shoulders balance tradition with innovation to drive growth, emphasizing deep consumer understanding and a blend of in-house innovation and strategic acquisitions. The article highlights P&G's commitment to consumer-centric product development, such as Head & Shoulders Bare, and the successful integration of acquired brands like Mielle while preserving their authenticity. Keith also touched on preserving brand heritage through modern campaigns and product forms to maintain relevance in the dynamic beauty market.

summary: P&G is committed to building a superior employee experience for its Business and Technical Associates (BTAs) by understanding their unique perspectives, fostering continued learning, and tailoring benefits to increase their sense of belonging. The company collaborates with Catalyst's Frontline Employee Initiative to improve attraction, retention, and satisfaction of frontline employees. P&G aims to create an inclusive workplace where all employees can thrive and contribute to their fullest potential, driving innovation and superior products.

title: Perrigo Appoints David Ball to the Newly Created Position of Executive Vice President and Chief Brand and Digital Officer
summary: Perrigo Company plc has appointed Dr. David Ball as Executive Vice President and Chief Brand and Digital Officer, a new role focused on enterprise-wide marketing strategy and brand-building. Dr. Ball brings extensive experience from Bayer Consumer Healthcare and Procter and Gamble, and his scientific background will contribute to innovation. This appointment aims to strengthen Perrigo's global over-the-counter business and support its blended-branded strategy.

title: Lil’ Drug Store Products Is Primary Distributor of Procter and Gamble’s Healthcare Products to Convenience Channel
summary: Lil’ Drug Store Products (LDSP) has become the primary distributor of Procter & Gamble’s healthcare products to the convenience channel, building on an existing partnership involving the Rolaids brand. This collaboration aims to significantly increase the accessibility of P&G's top healthcare SKUs in convenience stores, leveraging LDSP's sales, broker, and category management teams. The partnership is set to begin on September 3rd, with both companies anticipating boosts in distribution and revenue.

title: Lil’ Drug Store Products Becomes the Primary Distributor of Procter & Gamble’s Top Personal Healthcare Products to the Convenience Channel
summary: Lil’ Drug Store Products (LDSP) has announced its new role as the primary distributor of Procter & Gamble's (P&G) leading personal healthcare products to the convenience channel, building on an existing partnership that includes Rolaids. This collaboration, starting September 3, 2024, aims to enhance product accessibility and drive category growth for both companies. LDSP will leverage its sales, broker, and category management teams to support retail partners and maximize distribution and revenue for P&G's brands.

title: Kraft Heinz hires Hershey’s exec as chief sales officer
summary: Kraft Heinz has appointed Marlene Creighton, former chief sales officer at Hershey, as its new chief sales officer for U.S. retail. She will be responsible for overseeing the U.S. sales force and driving customer and channel growth, leveraging her two decades of CPG experience. This hire is part of Kraft Heinz's broader strategy to boost innovation and meet its goal of $2 billion in incremental net sales by 2027, amid other recent executive changes.

title: Procter & Gamble CEO Jon Moeller pay raised 6% to $23M
summary: Procter & Gamble CEO Jon Moeller's total compensation increased by 6% to $23 million in the last fiscal year, primarily due to additional stock options. This pay package makes him the highest-compensated CEO among Cincinnati's Fortune 500 companies, surpassing Kroger's Rodney McMullen and GE Aerospace's Larry Culp. The report also detailed the breakdown of his compensation, including an unchanged salary, a reduced bonus, increased stock awards, and various perks.

title: P&G Releases 2024 Annual Report
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has released its 2024 Annual Report, highlighting its integrated growth strategy focused on delivering superior products and creating value for all stakeholders. CEO Jon Moeller emphasized the company's commitment to consumers and the role of its empowered organization in driving growth. The report details five vectors of superiority and continuous improvement across operations.

title: P&G CFO talks revenue trends and how it can grow markets: ‘We understand what superiority means’
summary: Procter & Gamble's CFO, Andre Schulten, discussed the company's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue and future growth strategies at a recent investor presentation. Despite investor disappointment, Schulten sees the results as an opportunity to attract more customers, emphasizing P&G's understanding of product superiority. The article highlights P&G's approach to market growth and revenue trends.

title: Best Workplaces for Innovators 2024: Women innovators
summary: AtriCure has been recognized by Fast Company as the leading company for women innovators in its 2024 Best Workplaces for Innovators list. The medical device company earned this distinction after a new biomedical engineering graduate developed a less invasive clamp for cardiac ablation procedures, which has since treated over 10,000 patients. The article also lists other finalists for this recognition.

title: We Know Scented Pads and Tampons Aren’t Good for Vaginas. So Why Do Brands Still Offer Them?
summary: Despite medical advice against them, scented pads and tampons persist in the market, often due to ingrained societal shame around natural vaginal odor. Brands like Playtex and Always continue to offer "odor control" products, some with masking scents, contributing to confusion for consumers seeking truly fragrance-free options. Activists are pushing for stricter regulations and ingredient transparency, urging consumers to choose plain, unscented products for vaginal health.

title: E-News | Career Services hosts STEM Career Fair
summary: West Virginia University's Career Services is hosting a two-day STEM Career Fair on September 18-19, 2024, at the Student Rec Center. The event offers students opportunities to meet employers for full-time, part-time, and internship positions across various STEM fields. Short-term parking lots on the Evansdale campus will be closed to accommodate participating employers.

title: Procter & Gamble Announce $96.7M Investment in Louisiana Facility
summary: Procter & Gamble is investing $96.7 million to expand production capabilities at its Alexandria, Louisiana facility, which will create 15 new direct jobs and retain 572 existing positions. This investment will fund new production lines aimed at increasing overall capacity for products like Tide. Louisiana Economic Development provided an incentive package, including a $1 million grant, to facilitate this expansion.

title: P&G Announces $96 Million Expansion of Central Louisiana Fabric Care Product Manufacturing Facility
summary: Procter & Gamble is investing $96.7 million to expand its fabric care product manufacturing facility in Rapides Parish, Louisiana. This expansion is expected to create 15 new direct jobs and retain 572 current positions, with an additional 35 indirect jobs projected. The project, supported by a competitive incentives package from Louisiana Economic Development, will add new advanced production lines and increase capacity over the next two years.

title: Sensitive Toothpaste Market to Grow by USD 1.30 Billion (2024-2028), Driven by Innovations, Product Extensions, and AI Powered Market Transformation - Technavio
summary: The global sensitive toothpaste market is projected to grow by USD 1.30 billion between 2024 and 2028, accelerating at a CAGR of 8.09%. However, the market faces challenges from the widespread adoption of homemade remedies and alternative oral care products, particularly in developing countries.

title: P&G: Bio-AI for Enhanced Cold Water Cleaning
summary: Procter & Gamble has partnered with bio-AI start-up Basecamp Research to improve cold water laundry performance. This collaboration aims to develop new enzymes that work efficiently in cold temperatures, leveraging Basecamp Research's AI platform and genetic biodiversity data. The initiative supports P&G's sustainability goals, including their net zero emissions target by 2040, by enabling consumers to reduce energy consumption and lengthen clothing lifespan through cold water washing.

title: Smartsheet to go private in $8.4 bln deal with PE firms Vista and Blackstone
summary: Smartsheet will be taken private by Vista Equity Partners and Blackstone in an $8.4 billion deal, representing an 8.5% premium for investors. summary: This article covers the top five food retail industry news items, including Roger Wheeler's new leadership role at Stop & Shop, Kroger's ongoing court battles regarding its merger with Albertsons, a potential port strike impacting the U.S. food supply chain, Whole Foods' research into Gen Z consumer preferences, and Weis Markets' expansion in Pennsylvania through an acquisition.

summary: Procter & Gamble is investing $180 million in a major expansion of its St. Louis riverfront facility, which will create 100 new jobs. This expansion reinforces P&G's commitment to the local economy and its nearly centennial presence in St. Louis.

title: Procter & Gamble expansion creates jobs, investment in St. Louis
summary: Procter & Gamble has invested $180 million and created 100 new jobs with an expansion at its existing north St. Louis riverfront location. This expansion includes a new warehouse, new equipment, and conversion of an existing warehouse to a manufacturing facility, enhancing its operational efficiency and increasing production capacity. The company, which is approaching its 100th anniversary in St. Louis and produces brands like Cascade®, Mr. Clean®, and Febreze®, will benefit from the Missouri Works program.

title: Proctor & Gamble Opens New Expansion in North St. Louis
summary: Procter & Gamble has opened a new $180 million expansion in North St. Louis, which is expected to create 100 new jobs with an average salary of $65,000 and retain 530 existing positions. The project, approved in 2022, was a collaborative effort involving various St. Louis economic development entities and the Missouri Department of Economic Development. The expansion includes new amenities like a gym and a cafeteria focused on employee well-being.

title: 15 States Are Ordering The World's Weirdest "Candy" Choice For Halloween
summary: DoorDash data from 2023 reveals the most popular Halloween candies by state, with Reese's Peanut Butter Cups dominating in 24 states. Surprisingly, Gushers Tropical Fruit Flavored Snacks are the top choice in 15 states, while New Mexico's preference for Laffy Taffy Cherry Candy and Alabama's for Watermelon Sour Patch Kids stand out as unique. title: Procter & Gamble (PG) Suffers a Larger Drop Than the General Market: Key Insights
summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) experienced a larger drop than the general market, closing down 1.04% compared to the S&P 500's 0.96% loss. summary: Descendants of Procter & Gamble's founders failed in their bid to remove CEO Jon Moeller and members of the environmental sustainability committee. title: Inside the debate over PLA, the packaging industry’s favorite bioplastic
summary: Polylactic acid (PLA) is gaining popularity as a bioplastic for compostable packaging, with demand projected to grow significantly by 2032. title: Hershey Names Gene Kholodenko CIO
summary: Gene Kholodenko has been appointed as the CIO of The Hershey Company, where he will lead the company's tech modernization and digital transformation efforts. He brings over 26 years of experience, including a significant tenure at Procter & Gamble and McKesson, focusing on leveraging technology to drive business value across various functions. This appointment is part of Hershey's ongoing digital transformation journey, building on recent investments in analytics infrastructure and the hiring of its first CTO, Deepak Bhatia, to whom Kholodenko will report.

title: Procter & Gamble (PG) Q1 2025 Earnings: Key financials and quarterly highlights
summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) announced its Q1 2025 earnings, reporting net sales of $21.7 billion (down 1% YoY) and net earnings of $3.95 billion ($1.61 per share, down 12%). Despite decreased net sales, organic sales increased by 2%, and core EPS grew 5% to $1.93. The company provided fiscal year 2025 guidance, expecting modest sales and significant EPS growth.

title: Procter & Gamble earnings beat estimates, but weak demand in China hurts sales
summary: Procter & Gamble reported adjusted earnings per share that beat analyst expectations, but its revenue missed estimates due to weaker-than-expected sales. The company's organic sales in Greater China, its second-largest market, fell 15%, negatively impacting overall revenue despite growth in other segments. P&G provided a cautious outlook for China's recovery, expecting weakness to persist for several more quarters.

title: P&G Reports Weak Sales Growth on Lower Beauty, Baby Care Demand
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. reported a second consecutive quarter of sluggish sales growth, attributed to minimal price increases and weak demand in key categories like skin and baby care. Organic sales rose 2% in the fiscal first quarter, falling short of analyst projections, with prices increasing by only 1%. This performance was reportedly impacted by challenges in China and the Middle East, though the company maintained its sales outlook for the current fiscal year.

title: P&G posts surprise sales drop on slowing demand for face lotions, diapers
summary: Procter & Gamble reported a surprise drop in quarterly sales for the second consecutive time, primarily due to slowing consumer demand in the United States and China for products like face lotions and diapers. Despite the sales decline, P&G maintained its annual organic sales and core EPS forecasts, while analysts noted consumer sentiment impact from inflation and competition from cheaper brands. The company's CFO remains optimistic, planning new product launches and rejuvenations to sustain growth amid market challenges.

title: Kenvue shares surge after activist Starboard takes stake
summary: Activist investor Starboard Value has acquired a significant stake in Kenvue, prompting a 5% surge in Kenvue's share price. Starboard's Jeff Smith is expected to elaborate on their plans for Kenvue at an upcoming summit, just weeks after Starboard also amassed a $1 billion stake in Pfizer. Kenvue, which spun out of Johnson & Johnson in mid-2023, has seen its shares largely unchanged this year, with a market value currently around $41.6 billion.

title: Samir Singh Appointed as EVP Marketing for Colgate-Palmolive’s Asia-Pacific Division
summary: Samir Singh, a marketing veteran from Unilever, has been appointed as the Executive Vice President of Marketing for Colgate-Palmolive's Asia-Pacific division. He will take on this new role starting December 1, 2024, to lead the marketing strategy and bolster the company's brand presence and growth in the region. Singh previously held significant leadership positions at Unilever, including Chair of Unilever Asia.

title: Procter & Gamble reports decline in quarterly sales amid U.S. and China market challenges
summary: Procter & Gamble reported a second consecutive decline in quarterly sales, facing challenges from economic uncertainty in the U.S. and weak demand in China. Despite this, the company maintained its annual growth forecast. Sales were particularly affected in the baby, feminine, family care, and beauty segments, while P&G plans new product introductions to drive future growth.

summary: PureCycle Technologies, Inc. has terminated its joint venture with SK geo centric (SKGC) to build a polypropylene recycling facility in South Korea due to integration complexities. Despite the dissolution, both companies are open to future collaborations in South Korea. This decision comes amidst PureCycle's stock volatility, recent funding, and positive analyst ratings, though the company is not yet profitable.

summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has partnered with the Cincinnati Bengals to support local community initiatives, notably sponsoring the Bengals Girls Flag Football program. P&G, the world's largest consumer goods company, aims to further its commitment to supporting the communities where its employees live and work through this partnership.

title: Hamilton County magistrate approves 6 Frisch's Big Boy evictions
summary: A Hamilton County magistrate approved the eviction of six Frisch's Big Boy restaurants, giving them seven days to vacate the properties. The closures signify a challenging period for Frisch's, with further evictions anticipated.

summary: Stepan Company has appointed Luis E. Rojo as its new president and chief executive officer, effective immediately, succeeding Scott R. Behrens. Hinrichsen has been named interim CFO while a search for a permanent replacement is conducted.

title: U.S. FDA proposes ending use of popular decongestant present in cold medicines
summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has proposed to remove oral phenylephrine, a common decongestant in cold and cough syrups, from over-the-counter drugs due to its ineffectiveness. This decision follows a unanimous vote last year by an expert panel against its efficacy. While companies can continue marketing these products for now, the FDA will require reformulation or removal from the market, a move that the Consumer Healthcare Products Association has expressed disappointment over.

summary: The article ranks the top 100 consumer goods companies of 2024 based on fiscal year 2023 revenue, highlighting the top 10. summary: Procter & Gamble's Q1 2025 revenue declined slightly year-on-year, missing estimates, and net margin decreased due to higher non-operating expenses. title: Coty patents advanced eye cream with biodegradable surfactants
summary: Coty has patented an advanced eye cream formulation that utilizes biodegradable surfactants and aims to provide anti-aging and moisture benefits. The formulation emphasizes clean, consumer-friendly ingredients and a sophisticated blend of polyacrylates, boron nitride powder, and pearlescent pigments for enhanced texture, spreadability, and a "healthy-looking eye-zone area." This innovation highlights the industry trend towards high-performance, sustainable, and sensorially pleasing cosmetic products.

title: Increases to CEO Compensation Might Be Put On Hold For Now at The Clorox Company (NYSE:CLX)
summary: The Clorox Company's CEO Linda Rendle received total compensation of US$13m in 2024, an 8.9% increase from the previous year, which is above the industry median. Shareholders may consider delaying a CEO compensation raise until company performance improves, especially before the upcoming AGM on November 20th.

title: Procter & Gamble lands major site plan approval for manufacturing plant
summary: Procter & Gamble has received major site plan approval for the initial phase of its manufacturing plant in Pinal County, Arizona. title: Vanguard adds 3 funds to its ‘Investors Choice’ proxy voting program
summary: Vanguard has expanded its "Investors Choice" proxy voting program by adding three new funds. The move reflects a growing trend in asset management towards greater shareholder engagement.

summary: McCormick has appointed Guy Peri as its new chief information and digital officer, where he will oversee the company's digital transformation and enterprise IT strategy. Peri brings nearly 30 years of experience from Procter & Gamble, including roles as SVP and CIO of its global healthcare unit and its first chief data and analytics officer. His appointment aligns with McCormick's focus on integrating technology and innovation to drive growth and streamline operations, following recent initiatives like supply chain automation and a partnership with Cognizant for AI tool deployment.

title: P&G Progressing on $500M Coolidge Plant
summary: Procter & Gamble has committed to building a $500 million plant in Coolidge, Arizona, to produce fabric care brands. title: ICL Group to build EV battery component plant in north St. Louis
summary: ICL Group announced plans to construct a $547 million battery materials manufacturing plant in north St. Louis City, creating over 150 new jobs with an average salary exceeding $85,000. This facility will produce lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode active material for EV batteries. The project, supported by the Missouri Works program, aims to boost economic and residential growth in the area, with groundbreaking expected next year and opening in 2026.

title: Procter & Gamble doubles down on China’s TikTok to reverse sales slump
summary: Procter & Gamble (PG.N) is intensifying its marketing efforts on China's Douyin platform, the local version of TikTok, to combat a significant sales decline in the region. The company is revamping influencer strategies, improving marketing for products like Pantene, and building brand houses on Douyin to boost sales and regain market share amidst a sputtering Chinese economy and increased competition from local brands.

title: Procter & Gamble’s stock upgraded to buy as its China business is perking up
summary: D.A. Davidson has upgraded Procter & Gamble's stock to "buy" from "neutral" and increased its price target to $209 from $160 due to positive sales performance in China. summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) outlines its integrated growth strategy, centered on five key choices designed to delight and serve customers worldwide. title: New course to educate on cruelty-free testing
summary: Humane Society International, in collaboration with industry experts, has launched a free online master class called the Animal-Free Safety Assessment (AFSA) to train scientists on animal-free cosmetic and chemical testing methods. This multi-sector initiative aims to establish animal-free safety science as a global standard, offering more reliable results than animal-based testing. Major companies like Avon, L'Oréal, and Unilever have funded the course, which has already attracted over 1,200 participants from nearly 70 countries.

summary: The global household cleaning products market is projected to grow by USD 16.60 billion between 2024 and 2028, at a CAGR of 4.87%, driven by product innovation and portfolio expansion, alongside a rising demand for premium products. summary: Manish Anandani, MD of Kenvue India, discusses the company's strategic growth plans for the Indian consumer health market since its spin-off from Johnson & Johnson in 2023. summary: This article compares Coca-Cola and Procter & Gamble, both Dow Dividend Kings, to determine which is a better investment by the end of the year. Procter & Gamble, despite its strong capital return program and operating margins, trades above its historical P/E average, whereas Coke is below.

title: Onetime Procter & Gamble contractor ordered to pay $32 million for rent, utilities
summary: A former Procter & Gamble contractor, St. Bernard Soap Co., has been ordered to pay over $32 million for unpaid rent, utilities, and other expenses after ceasing operations earlier this year. The liabilities include a $1.35 million bill from Greater Cincinnati Water Works and $26 million for rent through its 20-year lease. title: The Science Behind Superior Products: From Insight to Innovation
summary: Procter & Gamble's Chief Research, Development and Innovation Officer, Victor Aguilar, highlights how deep consumer understanding, combined brand expertise, and advanced technology fuel the creation of superior products. The article showcases examples like the Swiffer PowerMop and the Perfume Development Digital Suite, demonstrating P&G's commitment to innovation and consumer-centric solutions. These innovations are part of P&G's Integrated Growth Strategy, aiming to solve everyday consumer problems more efficiently and effectively.

summary: This article celebrates the 100th anniversary of P&G Analytics & Insights, highlighting its foundational role in P&G's consumer-centric approach. title: Procter & Gamble to disclose wood-pulp audit details, investors say
summary: Procter & Gamble (PG.N) has committed to disclosing more details about its wood-pulp supplier audits following years of pressure from environmental-focused investors. This move comes after shareholders like Green Century pushed for more sustainable sourcing practices and raises scrutiny on logging's impact on the environment. P&G also agreed to invest $20 million in wood-pulp alternatives from 2025-2030 and recommitted to protecting Canada's untouched forests, with new information anticipated in mid-2025.

title: STATEMENT: Procter & Gamble commits to clarifying wood pulp sourcing policies
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has committed to clarifying its wood pulp sourcing policies, reiterating its goal to eliminate using resources from intact and primary forests, particularly in Canada's boreal forest. This decision follows discussions with investor groups including Green Century Capital Management, AXA Investment Managers, BNP Paribas Asset Management, and Robeco. In exchange, these investors withdrew a shareholder proposal asking P&G for enhanced disclosures on biodiversity and forest resilience risks.

title: Procter & Gamble Insiders Sell US$41m Of Stock, Possibly Signalling Caution
summary: Procter & Gamble insiders have sold a significant amount of stock, totaling US$41 million over the past year, which could signal caution to investors. While large insider sales can be ambiguous, multiple insiders selling shares might be a red flag. Despite high insider ownership, the lack of insider buying and recent selling suggest a cautious outlook for the company's stock.

title: P&G Earnings: Sales Slip but It Holds the Line on Prices
summary: Procter & Gamble reported a 1% slip in quarterly net sales, attributed to a weakened Chinese economy and Middle East conflict. Despite the sales decline, the company plans to maintain current pricing for its premium products in the U.S. These results were largely aligned with Wall Street's expectations.

title: An Interview with Alison Mass, Chairman, Investment Banking, The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc.
summary: Alison Mass, Chairman of Investment Banking at Goldman Sachs, discusses the firm's culture, values (partnership, client service, integrity, excellence), and industry leadership. She highlights her role in client relationships and leading the Office of Alumni Engagement, emphasizing the importance of diversity, community engagement, and mentoring future talent. Mass also shares her perspective on opportunities for women in the financial industry and the value of relationships in career development.

title: Procter & Gamble to invest $96.7 million to expand Pineville plant over two-year period
summary: Procter & Gamble announced a $96.7 million investment to expand its Rapides Parish facility in Pineville, Louisiana, over the next two years. This expansion will involve installing new advanced production lines and increasing capacity, creating 15 direct new jobs and retaining 572 existing positions. Louisiana Economic Development offered a competitive incentives package, including a $1 million performance-based grant, acknowledging P&G's 55-year commitment and significant contributions to the region's economy.

title: From Tide Pods to Coach bags, how Fortune 500 companies use museums of their hits and misses to drive success
summary: Fortune 500 companies are increasingly utilizing in-house museums and archives to drive success by learning from past product hits and misses. These collections, like P&G's "Wall of Failures" and Coach's handbag archive, serve practical purposes beyond nostalgia, guiding product development, C-suite decision-making, and culture-building among employees. The article highlights how brands like Delta, Walmart, Lego, Reckitt, and Coca-Cola leverage their histories to inspire innovation, foster a sense of purpose, and navigate challenges.

title: Cintas to upgrade Mason headquarters
summary: Cintas Corp. is investing $15 million to renovate its Mason headquarters and create 125 jobs, for which it has received a $2 million tax credit from the Ohio Tax Credit Authority. The renovation aims to enhance the work environment to attract and retain talent, incorporating natural light, outdoor work areas, and "innovation hubs." Cintas clarified that references to a "back-to-office" transition were inaccurate, as employees have been on-site for several years.

title: Digimarc Appoints Former Tide Cleaners CEO Katie Kool as Chairperson of its Board of Directors
summary: Digimarc Corporation has appointed Katie Kool, former CEO of Tide Cleaners, as the new Chairperson of its Board of Directors, effective June 10, 2024. Kool brings extensive experience in leading major brands to significant growth, including her role in expanding Tide Cleaners and profitably growing North America Fabric Care at Procter & Gamble. Her appointment is expected to help guide Digimarc through its next phase of growth and innovation, leveraging her financial acuity and industry understanding.

title: Supergoop! Appoints Beauty Industry Veteran Lisa Sequino as CEO to Lead Next Chapter of Growth
summary: Supergoop!, the SPF-focused skincare brand, has appointed Lisa Sequino as its new Chief Executive Officer. Sequino brings extensive experience from her previous role as CEO of JLo Beauty and nearly two decades at Estee Lauder and Procter & Gamble. This appointment aims to drive Supergoop!'s global expansion and innovation, building on its recent growth and strategic investments from Blackstone Growth and prominent investors.

title: Procter & Gamble lands major site plan approval for manufacturing plant
summary: Procter & Gamble has secured major site plan approval for the first phase of its manufacturing plant in Pinal County, Arizona, pushing forward with infrastructure work. The company plans a $500 million facility for fabric care brands, creating 500 jobs across 2 million square feet, though construction has not yet begun and its initial 2025 operational goal is unlikely to be met. P&G has already invested $53 million to acquire 430 acres for the project.

title: Scotts and P&G are facing off in federal court over product branding: What we know
summary: Scotts Miracle-Gro has filed a federal lawsuit against Procter & Gamble, alleging unfair competition and intellectual property infringement over P&G's new Spruce line of lawncare products. Scotts claims that Spruce's packaging, including its green and yellow color scheme, flowers, and circular logos, too closely resembles its Miracle-Gro brand, potentially causing consumer confusion and diluting Scotts' trade dress. A marketing expert emphasizes the critical role of packaging in brand identity and the potential for a new product with a similar look to take market share.

title: P&G to relocate hundreds of jobs, to close Winton Hill Business Center
summary: Procter & Gamble Co. is relocating approximately 1,500 jobs from its Winton Hill Business Center, which will close. About 300 jobs will move to its downtown Cincinnati headquarters by the end of 2024, with the remaining 1,200 relocating to its Mason campus starting in 2026. This move, spanning five years, aims to expand the Mason campus for innovation needs and best-in-class facilities.

title: Not A Year For The 2024 Dogs Of The Dow
summary: The article discusses the performance of the "Dogs of the Dow" strategy for 2024, noting that it was not a strong year for these high-dividend-yielding Dow Jones stocks. The company has signed a lease for 79,000 square feet on the entire 12th floor of Vornado Realty Trust’s 1290 Avenue of the Americas tower. This move represents a relocation from Oaktree's previous New York City office at Paramount Group's 1301 Avenue of the Americas.

title: Procter & Gamble accused of 'greenwashing' in Charmin toilet paper, lawsuit says
summary: Procter & Gamble is facing a new class-action lawsuit accusing it of "greenwashing" its Charmin toilet paper by misleading consumers with environmental claims. The lawsuit alleges that P&G sources most wood pulp for Charmin from the Canadian boreal forest through harmful logging practices, contrary to its public commitment to protecting the environment. Consumers are seeking restitution, compensatory and punitive damages, and an injunction to stop the alleged misleading claims.

title: Clearwater Paper to lay off 23 employees in Lewiston amid restructuring efforts
summary: Clearwater Paper announced layoffs of 23 employees at its Lewiston, Idaho mill and the elimination of 50 unfilled positions as part of a 10% global workforce reduction. This restructuring follows the sale of its tissue operations to Sofidel America Corp., allowing Clearwater Paper to focus on pulp and paperboard production. The company attributes the layoffs to high overhead costs and a downturn in the paperboard market, while committing to supporting affected employees and the Lewiston community.

title: P&G Meets Shifting Shopper Expectations With Household Staples, Digital Innovation
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) reported a 2% increase in net sales to $21.9 billion for Q2 2025, driven by growth in organic sales across various categories like beauty, grooming, healthcare, fabric and home care, and baby, feminine, and family care. The company attributes its success to a strong innovation program, a focus on consumer needs, and a thriving eCommerce presence, which helps it adapt to evolving consumer shopping behaviors. Despite challenges in markets like China, P&G reaffirmed its guidance for fiscal year 2025, expecting organic sales growth of 3-5% and core EPS growth of 5-7%.

title: Procter & Gamble earnings beat estimates as shoppers buy more household staples
summary: Procter & Gamble reported stronger-than-expected Q2 2025 earnings and revenue, driven by increased demand for household staples and improved sales in the U.S. and China. The company's volume rose 1% overall, despite some setbacks, and it reiterated its fiscal 2025 forecast. Shares increased more than 3% following the announcement.

summary: Medpace and Cintas were the most frequently chosen companies in the Cincinnati Business Courier's annual stock-picking contest. The ad, featuring dogs and a new version of "Who Let the Dogs Out," aims to target consumers thinking about spring lawn preparation. This approach allows P&G to avoid the high cost of a national Super Bowl slot while accelerating product awareness in key markets, with a wider national rollout planned later.

summary: Kimberly-Clark reported a quarterly sales decline and adjusted earnings per share that missed expectations, leading to a slight fall in shares. The company's earnings indicate that shoppers are willing to pay more for higher-quality versions of basic goods, buoyed by new adult and baby care items.

title: P&G Accused of Greenwashing and Creating ​“Frankenforests”
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Procter & Gamble (P&G), alleging the company is greenwashing by making misleading claims about the ethical sourcing and sustainable reforestation practices for its Charmin toilet paper. The plaintiffs accuse P&G of not truly protecting forests, creating environmentally damaging "Frankenforests" by replanting with single-species conifers and herbicides, and misusing FSC and Rainforest Alliance logos. The lawsuit contends these actions violate FTC Green Guides and highlights scrutiny companies face regarding environmental claims.

Smucker's ongoing portfolio optimization to focus resources on its Sweet Baked Snacks strategy, particularly growing the Hostess brand. title: WHY ARE MULTINATIONALS EXITING PAKISTAN? - Dawn
summary: Multinational Corporations (MNCs) are exiting Pakistan or scaling down operations due to a combination of global strategic shifts and a challenging local economic environment.
